newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks mixed in morning trade, HSBC strong.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks mixed in morning trade, HSBC strong.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were mixed on Wednesday morning, with banks firmer on the strength of HSBC shares while properties were weak after the government announced plans to boost land supply over coming years.
The Hang Seng Index was down 22 points, or 0.15 percent, to 15,464 after rising to a record high of 15,577.90.
"It's just HSBC and a few others. Blue chips are generally lower," said Peter Lui, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
HSBC Holdings shares jumped to a record HK$263.00 before falling back to HK$262.00. up HK$8.00.
"People are buying HSBC on its momentum. The bank is going to announce results in early August," Lui said.
Properties were lower after the government said it planned to boost residential land supply by 140 perceent in the five years to 2002 compared to the previous five years.
The Hang Seng properties sub-index was down 392 points, or 1.58 percent, to 24,427 in early trade.
Cheung Kong eased HK$1.00 to HK$75.75, Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.50 to HK$89.25 and Henderson Land was down HK$1.25 to HK$67.50.

James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings, said although property stocks were weak, the government's plans should provide a healthier property market, where prices have soared about 30 percent this year.
"I think we will actually see the whole market stabilising. You could say what we have at the moment is the best case scenario -- stable prices and volume created to meet demand," he said.
Hopewell Holdings fell HK$0.40 at HK$4.70 after it announced the sale of its remaining 19.99 percent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd to Southern Co.
